hero.lead: I develop Flow Network Models and Digital Twins for large-scale data center liquid cooling systems — working with NVIDIA, Vertiv, and Villanova University on the ARPA-E OMNICOOL project to model single- and two-phase direct-to-chip cooling for high-power GPU racks.

about.title: About Me
paragraphs: I'm a graduate researcher in the Department of Mechanical Engineering at Villanova University, working under Dr. Alfonso Ortega in the Laboratory for Advanced Thermal and Fluid Systems. My research focuses on Flow Network Modeling (FNM) and Digital Twin development for large-scale, high-power data center cooling systems.

I lead the development of a two-phase component library (cold-plates, quick disconnects, flow regulators, heat exchangers) in the Flownex Simulation Environment, and integrate these models into an interactive Digital Twin built on NVIDIA Omniverse — connecting physics-based simulation, live telemetry, and even XR control via Apple Vision Pro.

items.title: OMNICOOL — Two-Phase Cooling POD (ARPA-E)
items.text: A 250 kW self-contained, containerized POD with a clear scaling path to 1 MW+, demonstrated live at the ARPA-E Energy Innovation Summit. End-to-end two-phase pumped refrigeration (R515B heat rejection / R1234yf at the chip) achieves ~0.005°C/W package thermal resistance, PUE below 1.05, and zero water consumption at ≥40°C ambient. Built with Vertiv, Boyd (Eaton), Binghamton University, and Villanova University, integrated with a physics-based NVIDIA Omniverse Digital Twin.

items.title: Two-Phase Data Center Component Library
items.text: Cold-plates, quick disconnects, flow regulators, and two-phase heat exchangers developed in the Flownex Simulation Environment and validated against experimental test data (e.g. Kandlikar two-phase cold-plate model).

items.title: Single-Phase vs. Two-Phase Cooling Comparison
items.text: Transient simulation of identical server racks under a 40%→100% heat-load spike; the two-phase system showed a 30% lower chip case-temperature rise (29.5°C vs. 42.1°C) due to latent-heat cooling.

items.title: XR Remote Control Interface (Apple Vision Pro)
items.text: Immersive control panel for the Digital Twin — IT load, ambient temperature, fan speed, and altitude set directly in XR and streamed to the Omniverse simulation via a structured command/telemetry layer.
